result.title: Generated storm lifecycles fill the rare-event tail of short rainfall records
result.summary: Historically rare ''one-in-a-generation'' storms are occurring with unprecedented frequency, causing catastrophic damage and mounting casualties, and exposing the vulnerability of infrastructure designed around short observational records. To overcome the limitations of sparse data, we present StormGen, a generative machine-learning model that transforms an observed storm's initial hours into complete, physically plausible hourly rainfall lifecycles in minutes. Evaluated on a decade of southeast Texas rainfall, StormGen produced close counterparts for 4\5% of the most severe 2\% of storms--compared to just 3\% for stochastic storm transposition--and maintained spatial coherence over full 24-hour sequences. Crucially, from a single hour of initial rainfall, the model successfully reconstructed the specific lifecycle, spatial pattern, and extreme catchment totals of Hurricane Harvey itself, despite the event being entirely absent in training. Because storm timing alone can more than double peak flows, these complete generated scenarios provide a vital mechanism to stress-test flood protections against unprecedented extremes.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 StormGen 生成式模型，将实测风暴最初几小时的降雨转化为完整的 24 小时逐时降雨生命周期，用于补足短观测记录中极端事件的稀疏尾部，并以德州东南部数据及 Harvey 事件做评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于气象领域的条件生成与极端事件外推应用，虽涉及由部分观测生成完整序列，但未涉及多模态视觉表示、推理状态更新、证据筛选或停止决策等 LVR 问题，缺乏可核查的方法借鉴线索。
